detail.longDescription: AI is changing the way companies hire. Resume screening, candidate matching, assessments, interview scheduling, and candidate communication can now be supported by AI. But there’s a question I keep coming back to: Just because we can automate something, should we? I work in AI and HR technology, and one thing I’ve noticed is that the interesting part isn’t automation itself. It’s deciding where automation actually helps people. Where AI can help There are many parts of hiring that are repetitive and time-consuming: Reading hundreds of resumes Finding relevant skills and experience Organizing candidate information Identifying patterns across assessments Generating structured summaries Reducing repetitive administrative work These are areas where AI can give recruiters and hiring teams more time. But hiring isn’t just data A candidate isn’t simply a collection of keywords, scores, or previous job titles. There is context behind the information. A hiring manager might need to understand: How someone approaches problems How their experience fits the role What they could learn next How they communicate Whether additional context changes the interpretation of their results These are areas where human judgment still matters. The approach I find interesting Instead of thinking about: AI vs. humans I think about: AI + humans AI can help collect, organize, and surface relevant signals. Humans can provide context, ask better questions, and make the final judgment. That creates a different approach to automation: Automate the work. Keep the judgment human. I’m currently exploring this intersection through my work in AI and HR technology, and I’m interested in how developers and product teams are approaching similar questions in other industries. Where do you think AI should draw the line between automation and human decision-making? I’d love to hear how others here are thinking about it. ai # generativeai # hrtech # discuss # ai # automation # career # productivity # software # coding # development # engineering # inclusive # community AI in Hiring: What Should We Automate, and What Should Stay Human?
